blocks.content: Pod anti-affinity is the direct opposite of pod affinity, scheduling a Pod away from other Pods matching a selector, the standard mechanism for spreading replicas apart for real high availability.
Where pod affinity pulls Pods together, anti-affinity deliberately pushes them apart, expressing "do not schedule this Pod near other Pods matching this selector."

blocks.alt: A rule that deliberately keeps matching Pods apart, not together

blocks.content: 2. The Classic Use Case: High Availability
blocks.text: 2. The Classic Use Case: High Availability

blocks.content: This is the mechanism behind a genuinely important production practice: spreading a Deployment's replicas across different nodes (or different availability zones), so a single node or zone failure cannot take down every replica at once.

blocks.alt: Every replica on the same node defeats the entire point of having several

blocks.content: Exactly as with pod affinity, a topologyKey defines the scope "away" applies to, spreading replicas across nodes and spreading them across entire availability zones are both configured the same way, just with a different topology key.

blocks.alt: The same topologyKey mechanism, now defining the scope of separation

blocks.content: The same required-versus-preferred distinction applies here too, a hard anti-affinity rule genuinely refuses to co-locate matching Pods, a soft one tries to spread them, but will still schedule a Pod even if perfect separation is not currently achievable.

blocks.alt: A hard refusal, or a soft, best-effort attempt at separation

blocks.content: 5. A Real Example: Spreading Deployment Replicas
blocks.text: 5. A Real Example: Spreading Deployment Replicas

blocks.content: A Deployment's Pod template commonly includes anti-affinity against its own label, ensuring the scheduler actively avoids placing two replicas of the same Deployment on the same node.

blocks.alt: A Deployment actively keeping its own replicas apart from each other

blocks.content:
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        podAffinityTerm:
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: my-app
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Pod anti-affinity schedules a Pod away from other Pods matching a selector, the standard tool for spreading replicas across nodes or zones for real HA.
It shares the same topologyKey and required/preferred mechanics as pod affinity, just applied in the opposite direction, pushing apart instead of pulling together.
